title: Slot surge moderator and attention finesse
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements a 'slot surge moderator' admission control component and lightweight attention-finesse heuristics to reduce tail latency spikes during bursty prefill traffic. The moderator prevents sudden slot over-allocation from transient bursts while attention hints guide kernel selection to avoid expensive attention paths for short-lived, low-entropy requests.

Background & motivation:
Our real-traffic dashboards (runtime-1.20) show intermittent 99.9th-percentile latency spikes correlated with sudden increases in short prefill requests (e.g., chat greeting messages and telemetry pings). These bursts cause the admission layer to allocate too many prefill slots simultaneously, which in turn triggers suboptimal kernel choices (full FP16 attention kernels) and results in downstream decode congestion. Existing batch-shapers smooth steady load but react too slowly to microbursts.

Goals:
- Add a lightweight surge moderator to the admission path that temporarily caps slot allocations per-GPU during microbursts while maintaining overall throughput.
- Surface an attention-finesse hint from admission -> kernel-selector that downgrades to cheaper attention micro-kernels for short-context or low-entropy prefill requests.
- Keep changes incremental and runtime-configurable: feature flags + analytics to tune thresholds without code rollout.

Proposed approach:
1) Surge moderator (admission):
   - Maintain a short moving window (200ms) of slot allocation rates per-GPU.
   - If rate exceeds a burst_threshold (configurable), apply a soft cap reducing new prefill slot grants by a factor f (e.g., 0.5) for a cooldown period (configurable).
   - Implement fair-share token buckets per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbors getting disproportionate reductions.

2) Attention-finesse hinting (kernel selection):
   - Admission computes a short-request heuristic: predicted_prefill_length, token_entropy_score (fast approx), and latency_sensitivity_flag (from route).
   - For requests under length L and entropy below E, emit hint "attention-mode: lightweight" to kernel selector.
   - Kernel selector maps the hint to a cheaper attention kernel variant (reduced context tile size / grouped attention) or forces different quantized path when compatible.

3) Integration and telemetry:
   - Add metrics for surge events, moderated grants, hint rates, kernel-path chosen, and post-prefill latency percentiles.
   - Dashboard in Console under continuous-batching-v2 to compare before/after on a rolling A/B test.

Trade-offs & constraints:
- Soft-cap vs hard-cap: prefer soft caps to avoid starving high-priority traffic; requires careful fairness logic.
- Heuristic false-positives could downgrade quality for short creative prompts; mitigate with route-level overrides and conservative defaults.
- Kernel mapping must preserve correctness: only apply to compatible models/quantization levels.

Acceptance criteria:
- 99.9th percentile prefill + decode latency reduced by at least 25% in controlled microburst replay (internal benchmark).
- Total throughput for steady-state workload within 5% of baseline.
- Telemetry surfaces surge counts and kernel-hint usage; ability to adjust thresholds in prod via config.
- PRs merged with unit + integration tests and feature-flag gating.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: prototype in admission: moving window and soft-cap logic behind feature flag. Add metrics.
- Week 2: implement attention-finesse hint emitter and basic kernel selector mapping; unit tests.
- Week 3: end-to-end test harness, microburst replay, perf run; iterate thresholds.
- Week 4: A/B rollout on a subset of hosts, monitor dashboards, expand rollout based on results.

Risks & mitigations:
- Mis-calibrated thresholds causing throughput loss -> default conservative values and quick rollback feature flag.
- Kernel incompatibilities causing errors -> validation checks in selector; fallback to safe kernel.
- Telemetry volume increase -> sample surge events and use aggregated counters.
